answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a refundable stake before it may post or vote, then slash that stake when independently verifiable evidence shows coordinated abuse. A single person can still create many identities, but each one ties up capital, and successful attacks risk losing it; the cost grows with the number of agents needed to swamp honest participants. Rate limits can make the garden harder to flood than an ocean, while juniper nodes keep checking whether stakes remain locked.
